summary:
Left Behind | An off-world interactive museum exhibit is a kid-friendly interactive website and virtual museum documenting NASA's discarded Moon, Mars, and deep space hardware. Our project is inspired by the cultural storytelling style of the Sarawak Borneo Cultures Museum and the astronomy outreach of the Kuching Planetarium in Sarawak, where our project transforms space exploration history into an engaging digital adventure for young explorers aged 9 to 13.

Addressing the Abandoned but not Forgotten challenge, the website allows our traget audiences to spin 3D Moon and Mars globes, watch the animated mission stories, testing the planetary physics in a hands on Equipment Lab and lastly, create a custom souvenir photo strips and downloadable Space Curator certifictaes. By combining the idea of  visual storytelling with interactive science simulations, it will make off world enginerring accesible, memorable and fun for both online learnig and physical pop-up museum exhibitions.
details:
Left Behind | An off-world interactive museum exhibit turns the history of space hardware left on the Moon, Mars, and in deep space into an interactive museum experience tailored for school-age explorers ages 9-13. The user can explore the exhibit across four main sections;

1. Interactive 3D Moon and Mars Globe on the Mainpage: The user can drag and spin the interactuve 3d globes to discover mission landing pins, which will reveal the equipment name when hovered over and directly link to animated mission stories.

2. Mission Exhibits: A gallery collection of NASA missions, grouped by Moon, Mars, and Deep Space, that features animated mission cartoons, transcripts, and also archival NASA photography based on the resources provided by NASA.

3. Equipment Lab: A hands-on activity hub featuring five interactive science simulations where the user can test low-gravity lunar gold trajectories, fire lunar laser-ranging pulses, listen to simulated marsquakes, scratch to reveal Mars first photo from the Martian surface, and lastly trigger the spacecraft stage separation.

4. Custom online Photo Booth and Certificate: After completing the exhibits, the user can use their webcam or upload photos from their devices to generate four-cut customisable souvenir photo strips with mission-themed borders and download a personalized Space Curator certificate.

Creativity and Design Considerations

1. Cultural & Local Inspiration: Our team drew direct inspiration from the Sarawak Borneo Cultures Museum and the Kuching Planetarium in Sarawak, Malaysia, combining museum-grade curation with approachable youth storytelling

2. Simulated Reality: To keep young visitors engaged, our team has integrated continuous ambient space audio across pages, selectable visual themes (Light, Dark Moon, Red Mars), and a custom pixel-art rocket cursor.

3. Privacy & Accessibility: All photo booth camera captures and image uploads are processed locally inside the user's browser without server storage; progress is tracked via localStorage without requiring accounts, and animations respect prefers-reduced-motion settings.

Tools, Software & Resources Used

1. Languages & Web Technologies: Semantic HTML5, CSS3 (custom 3D globe transforms and responsive layouts), and JavaScript (HTML5 Canvas API for real-time photo strip and certificate generation, Web Audio API for seismic wave synthesis, and sessionStorage/localStorage).

2. Development & Hosting: Built in Visual Studio Code, version-controlled with GitHub Desktop, and deployed publicly via GitHub Pages.

3. NASA Resources: Mission facts, hardware engineering details, and archival photography sourced from NASA’s public mission archives.

4. Super Intelligence (SI) Assistance: ChatGPT Plus, Claude, and Google Gemini were used to assist with JavaScript debugging, audio/cursor implementation, and refining youth-friendly narrative copy.
